figures.caption: Fig. 5: t-SNE visualization of feature embeddings on the Test Set. (a) ProtoNet (λ = 0.00): The projection reveals severe entanglement between Glioma (Blue) and Meningioma (Orange). (b) Proposed (λ = 0.15): The injection of deterministic chaotic noise geometrically reorganizes the manifold, forcing cluster centroids apart and tightening intra-class variance.
Fig. 4: Comparative confusion matrices demonstrating the regularizing effect of the Logistic Chaos Module.

Fig. 1: Conceptual framework of embedding space stabilization. (a) Standard ProtoNet: Inherent feature noise in data-scarce regimes drives high intra-class variance, leading to overlapping clusters and displacement in centroid. (b) Proposed CEProtoNet: The integration of a Logistic Chaos Module (purple trajectory) during training works as a deterministic regularizer and forces the architecture to resolve a continuous manifold of simulated variations, thereby sharpening decision boundaries and establishing robust, noise-resilient prototypes.

Fig. 6: Qualitative assessment of model predictions. Top Row (Successes): Correct classifications. Bottom Row (Failures): The model struggles with diffuse Gliomas, frequently misclassifying them as Meningiomas.
Table 1: Comparison of classification performance across varying Chaos Intensities (λ).
Fig. 3: Performance trajectory of test accuracy across an various chaos intensities.

Fig. 2: Architectural overview of the Chaos-Enhanced Prototypical Network (CEProtoNet). The framework Uses a pretrained ResNet-18 backbone with a Selective Fine-Tuning strategy (frozen early layers, trainable deep layers). The Logistic Chaos Module (LCM) introduces deterministic noise into the Support embeddings to create robust prototypes, while Query images bypass the chaos injection to ensuring deterministic inference.
